item.title: US investigating if missile hit Iran wedding, Vance says
item.description:
US Central Command has released footage that purportedly shows missile and drone strikes being fired at Iranian military targets. Footage of some of the aftermath of the US attacks was shared on social media, showing shrapnel damage on a home in Sirik, southern Iran, where a wedding celebration was taking place. Since publication of this video, Iranian state media has revised the death toll to four people. Iran retaliated shortly afterwards, with video shared by Iranian media said to show missiles being fired towards Jordan. A US Central Command spokesperson said the US was aware of reports of civilian casualties, but that the 'US military never targets civilians, unlike the IRGC [Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps]' Iran accuses US of ‘war crime’ after missile blast kills five people at wedding Continue reading...

item.title: Why are people calling Venezuela oil deal a new form of US colonialism?
item.description:
Just days after the U.S. military captured Venezuelan dictator Nicolás Maduro in early January, Secretary of State Marco Rubio outlined the Trump administration's plans for the future of the South American country. Rubio described a three-stage process. First would be "stabilization of the country," which would include President Donald Trump's biggest priority: seizing oil reserves. "We are going to take between 30 and 50 million barrels of oil," Rubio said in January. Then would come the latter stages of the plan, which Rubio described as "recovery" (opening up Venezuelan markets) and, lastly, a political "transition" toward new leaders. Those remarks—and the order of Rubio's priorities—are worth revisiting in light of last week's announcement that the U.S. would be, in President Trump's terms , taking "control of more than 65 BILLION BARRELS of proven Oil Reserves in Venezuela."…

item.title: Tributes to Gloria Steinem are flooding in, from Hollywood to Capitol Hill
item.description:
Glowing obituaries are pouring in after the death of feminist icon Gloria Steinem, who was born in 1934. The Associated Press called her “a potent voice of US feminism,” and the Washington Post heralded her as the “lodestar of the modern women’s movement.” It is hard to overstate her influence upon Western women. Gloria Steinem wasn’t just one among many feminists; she was the “it” girl who normalized feminism and made it broadly attractive. Prior to her arrival on the scene, the movement was populated by angry, cantankerous, and mentally ill women whose irascibility made them difficult to work with: Kate Millett was mentally ill and an “out” bisexual; Angela Davis was an angry Black Panther; and Betty Friedan wasn’t the kind of woman other women dreamed of being like. And then came Gloria. Her long blond tresses, aviator glasses, and lithe physique opened the door to a new chapter for…

item.title: Tunisia’s top court upholds conviction of opposition figures, activists
item.description:

item.title: NBA hits LA Clippers with a record fine for circumventing salary cap
item.description:
The league is awash with ultra-wealthy owners. Adam Silver is hoping a hefty punishment for the Clippers will send them a message about who is in charge When Steve Ballmer bought the Los Angeles Clippers for $2bn in 2014, it was widely regarded as a coup for the NBA. Not only is Ballmer one of the richest men in the world – worth an estimated $152.7bn – but his passion and enthusiasm for the sport stood in stark contrast to the team’s embattled former owner. Donald Sterling, who bought the Clippers for $12.5m in 1981, was forced to sell after being handed a lifetime ban by the NBA in response to a series of racist comments . Continue reading...
